videos.title: In the Studio: Roberta Gambarini, Part 3
videos.description:
Roberta Gambarini talks about playing her first jazz festival in Cape Town and meeting James Moody.

This April 27-29, the Jazz at Lincoln Center Orchestra with Wynton Marsalis celebrates the centennial of Ella Fitzgerald, a vocalist whose legacy and influence define a classic era of jazz singing. Through diverse repertoire arranged by the Jazz at Lincoln Center Orchestra, tonight's guest vocalists will demonstrate why the "First Lady of Song" remains a case study in succinct phrasing and uncompromising musicality. Joining the Orchestra for this special occasion are two celebrated veteran vocalists: Kenny Washington and Roberta Gambarini. Washington–Ravi Coltrane's favorite vocalist–carries on Ella's legacy by finding the maximum impact in each and every song, utilizing his enormous range and improvisational skills with restraint and impeccable taste. Gambarini–a similarly tasteful yet boldly original artist–was described by NEA Jazz Master Hank Jones as "the best new jazz singer to come along in 50 years." In Ella Fitzgerald's centennial year, you will witness how her most identifiable traits and her complete devotion to originality and authenticity inspire the best musicians of our time.

videos.title: In the Studio: KURT ELLING, Part 2
videos.description:
What does jazz mean to KURT ELLING? Watch and find out. 

See Kurt Elling with the Branford Marsalis Quartet at Jazz at Lincoln Center this Jan. 20-21: http://ow.ly/jEOF30882os 

In an unprecedented collaboration, the Branford Marsalis Quartet welcomes vocalist Kurt Elling, a rare addition to the rock-solid lineup of Joey Calderazzo, Eric Revis, and Justin Faulkner. Both parties are known for a wealth of jazz knowledge and stylistic versatility. Elling has repeatedly proven his prowess for working with star instrumentalists and quartets, recently winning a Grammy Award for his tribute to the famed collaboration between saxophonist John Coltrane and vocalist Johnny Hartman. Marsalis, too, is a flexible and ambitious artist; best known as a prolific jazz leader and sideman to such icons as Miles Davis, Art Blakey, and Dizzy Gillespie, he is also renowned for his work in classical music and for crossover collaborations with artists including Sting and The Grateful Dead. For this special occasion, the band will perform selections from its Grammy-nominated debut release, Upward Spiral (Marsalis Music). Featuring fresh arrangements of Songbook staples, jazz standards, and standards-to-be from a diverse array of composers, this new artistic alliance promises to be an unforgettable showcase of both instrumental and vocal jazz expertise.

videos.title: Buy the LIVE IN CUBA vinyl box set from Amazon
videos.description:
The deluxe, 4-LP vinyl edition of LIVE IN CUBA is available from Amazon now: http://ow.ly/79sl305nPz8

From bebop to bolero and beyond, LIVE IN CUBA captures nine-time Grammy Award-winning Wynton Marsalis and the world-renowned Jazz at Lincoln Center Orchestra with Wynton Marsalis's first—and only—performances in Cuba. Explore the profound connections between American jazz and Afro-Cuban music on this deluxe vinyl box set, out 10/28. It features four LPs, a gorgeous booklet, and a download of the album plus a never-before-released song: Oo Na Ney, performed by the Wynton Marsalis Quintet with Chucho Valdes & the Afro-Cuban Messengers.

Recorded in front of clamorous, sold-out crowds over three nights at Havana's Mella Theatre in October 2010, LIVE IN CUBA finds the Jazz at Lincoln Center Orchestra with Wynton Marsalis performing Ellington standards, Afro-Cuban numbers, and distinctly modern compositions from band members. LIVE IN CUBA is a document of two nations’ indelible cultural connections and of an emotional reunion between long-lost musical cousins.

videos.title: In the Studio: STEVE MILLER, Part 3
videos.description:
Guitarist, vocalist, and Jazz at Lincoln Center board member Steve Miller discusses his first meeting with Wynton Marsalis and how he first got involved with Jazz at Lincoln Center. Come see his shows, entitled  "T-Bone Walker: A Bridge From Blues to Jazz,"  this December 9-10!

Renowned blues-rock guitarist, singer/songwriter, and lifelong jazz fan Steve Miller returns to Jazz at Lincoln Center for an in-depth look at T-Bone Walker. Considered the founding father of electric blues guitar, Walker changed the way blues was played with his unique and extraordinary solo electric guitar performances. Miller learned his first chords at age five from his godfather Les Paul, how to play lead guitar from T-Bone Walker at age nine, and how to perform from some of the best bluesmen in Chicago (including Muddy Waters, Howlin' Wolf, Buddy Guy, Paul Butterfield, and James Cotton) has incorporated his affinity for the blues into all of his major recordings, and is now working closely with Jazz at Lincoln Center to explore and expand upon authentic blues styles. Joined by blues all-star Jimmie Vaughan, B-3 organist Mike Flanigin, rising star vocalist Brianna Thomas, pianist Shelly Berg, alto saxophonist/clarinetist Patrick Bartley, tenor saxophonist Craig Handy, baritone saxophonist Lauren Sevian, trumpeter Mike Rodriguez, bassist Yasushi Nakamura, and former Earth Wind & Fire drummer Sonny Emory, Miller has chosen music that takes audiences across the bridge from blues to jazz.

videos.title: Richard Smallwood – "Hebrews 11" (Rare Original Demo) | From the Personal Archive
videos.description:
In 2014, I had the extraordinary privilege of spending a week with the legendary Richard Smallwood while producing The Richard Smallwood Singers Documentary at his request. During that time, Richard invited me into his creative world and played this early demo of what would eventually become part of his Hebrews 11 live recording. I was so captivated by it that I asked if I could have a copy, and he graciously shared it with me.

Years later, while revisiting my personal archives, I rediscovered this recording and was immediately reminded of the brilliance I witnessed firsthand. Today, I'm honored to share this rare glimpse into the creative process of one of the most prolific composers, arrangers, and musicians in the history of Gospel music. My hope is that it not only preserves a small piece of Richard's extraordinary legacy but also offers inspiration to future generations of musicians, worshippers, and lovers of Gospel music.

videos.title: Afropop Worldwide Living Room Session #4 | Razia
videos.description:
We are happy to share Living Room Session #4, part of Afropop’s series of live performances recorded in living rooms, homes and music studios around New York City.
On a warm summer morning, Malagasy-born singer and songwriter Razia Said welcomed us into her Harlem apartment for an intimate and uplifting set.
A longtime New Yorker, Razia writes and sings mostly in Malagasy, drawing on the rhythms, melodies and instruments she grew up with to address environmental destruction in Madagascar, resilience and homecoming. 

For this session, Razia takes us through songs from different moments in her career, including the albums Akory (2015) and The Road (2018). The opening track, “Zanako,” from Akory, means “my child” in Malagasy and looks toward the children of Madagascar as the country’s future. “Mbola Velogno, ” written for her latest album, The Road, means “still alive.” The song carries the same unshakable sense of hope that sits at the heart of much of Razia’s work. 

MUSICIANS
Razia Said: Vocals
David Rajaonary: Guitar, vocals
Harvey Wirht: Drums, vocals
Zwelakhe-Duma Bell le Pere: Bass

videos.title: NEW @AFROPOPWORLDWIDE LIVING ROOM SESSION: Alsarah & Brandon Terzic at Barzakh Cafe
videos.description:
Watch and be transported: bit.ly/alsarahsession

@Alsarah5000 of @alsarahandthenubatones, Sudanese-American singer, songwriter, and ethnomusicologist joined New York-based multi-instrumentalist and composer @terzicbrandon who plays oud and ngoni with Alsarah & the Nubatones. Together, they played songs at @barzakh.cafe composed by Egyptian Nubian composer and oud master Hamza El Din in both Arabic and Nubian.

Alsarah brings a plaintive depth and cross-cultural resonance in her vocals that undulate over the timeless, ancient, and influential oud – expertly played by Terzic.

For the full songs including lyrics, translations and more, head to afropop.org.

“Cutlure is made up. We make up culture, therefore we control culture.” –Alsarah

videos.title: Afropop Living Room Sessions: Kotoko Brass and Mohammed Alidu
videos.description:
For this second Afropop Living Room Session, Kotoko Brass is joined by Ghanaian musician Mohammed Alidu, who sings and performs on the lunga talking drum, a traditional instrument of northern Ghana. 

Kotoko Brass brings together the traditional drumming of central Ghana, Caribbean rhythm section grooves, and the bright horn energy of New Orleans to create what the Boston Globe has called “propulsive, infectious party music.” 

The band was founded by brothers Ben and Brian Paulding and includes master Ghanaian percussionists Attah Poku and Kwame Ofori alongside a seasoned rhythm and horn section. 

The collaboration brings together musical traditions from different regions of Ghana in a performance grounded in rhythm, dance, and collective celebration.

videos.title: Afropop Living Room Sessions: Aba Diop & the Yermande Family
videos.description:
We are proud to introduce the first edition of the Afropop Worldwide Living Room Sessions. This edition features Aba Diop and the Yermande Family, a band that blends Senegalese traditions--Wolof, Mande and more--in a thrilling ensemble presentation. The band was formed in Dakar, Senegal, but now has a second home in the U.S. This session was recorded amid the band's tour to promote their 2025 album, Family.  

Aba Diop is a master of the sabar drum, the beating heart of Senegal’s most popular dance music: mbalax. The percussive center of the Yermande Family is Diop’s fiery duo volleys with tama player Samba Ndokh, a veteran of Cheikh Lo’s band. Noumoukunda Cissoko on kora brings the Mande music element to the band, while griot vocalist Zeyna Ngom Diop delivers commanding lead vocals, often joined by Aba Diop and Samba Ndokh. Guitarist Jason Hosier, the one American in the band, has spent significant time learning guitar styles in Senegal, and it shows.

This is a band that can command every inch of a concert stage, with kinetic moves, dramatic dancing and irresistible ambiance. Here we find them in the at-home setting, seated, at ease and relaxed, but no less electrifying.

Mokoomba’s Unforgettable Return to London
After 6 years since the legendary Mokoomba last played in London, they finally made their very special appearance at the Jazz Cafe, in Camden Town. And there is no better place to perform than this brilliant, intimate venue. Three words to describe this musical experience would be playful, entertaining, and healing. It might be one of the most unique and enjoyable live events the Jazz Cafe has seen. It appeared the crowd had already anticipated this, as the audience began streaming an eager hour and a half before the scheduled start time to secure themselves a prime spot in the crowd. In January 2000, having survived Y2K, Afropop Worldwide's Banning Eyre met American music legend Howard Armstrong (1909-2003) in his apartment in Boston, where he was living at age 92 with his companion and fellow musician Barbara Ward. The talk went long, far more than could fit in the APWW episode The African American String Music Tradition, encored for Black History Month 2023. 
This is an audio edit of their conversation that day.

videos.title: Natu Camara Building Bridges from Harlem to Conakry
videos.description:
The star is rising for independent female singer songwriter and guitarist Natu Camara and she’s on a mission to be the best version of herself and elevate and educate the world about girls through her foundation Dimedi, new music festival Harlem Meet Africa. Pioneer member of the first all female R & B and hip hop band in West Africa, The Ideal Black Females, Natu is inspired to build bridges through bringing together the community of Harlem with the power of music.  From Guinea Conakry, the epicenter of a brilliant music scene, Natu and her band are bringing this African musical renaissance to Harlem New York City.  This is a free artist on fire with clear objectives and a musical songbook that spans the black Atlantic.  Her latest single Farre, delivers on her promise to embrace all aspects of her spiritual self that includes, using  12th century Mandinka rhythms remixed with rock and roll and every black genre in between. The video to the song titled “Farré”, which means “the dance” in Soussou, lingua franca of the capital of Guinea (Conakry), is cementing this new culturally specific image of Africa she champions. The complex beat will have you on your toes and in in perpetual movement and just like nature itself, Natu is a force and we are fans forever. Support her girls academy#dimedi #natucamara #afropopworldwide #mukwaewabeisiyolwe #seanbarlow #banningeyre #worldmusicproductions 

Mukwae Wabei Siyolwe of Afropop sat down Natu over morning coffee on Zoom.

This Afropop Worldwide program draws on 20 years of interviews with the man, and expert analysis from Congolese music aficionado Lubangi Muniania. Produced by Banning Eyre.

videos.title: An Encounter With the Ancestors: Yougouda
videos.description:
Hear the full episode via Afropop.org: https://afropop.org/audio-programs/encounter-with-the-ancestors

For over 10 years, Eric Nelson Efa and members of his association, the Azania Way Culture, have crisscrossed almost half of Cameroon's 10 regions: the deep north around Lake Chad; the central region, the Adamawa; and the south, to record traditional musicians who are getting very old and are the last repository of traditional music in Cameroon. In this episode of Afropop Worldwide, “Encounter With the Ancestors,” Georges Collinet takes us to Eric’s village in the deep forest of southern Cameroon to listen to his story. We also meet young musicians influenced by the art of their ancestors, including an opera singer!

For over 10 years, Eric Nelson Efa and members of his association, the Azania Way Culture, have crisscrossed almost half of Cameroon's 10 regions: the deep north around Lake Chad; the central region, the Adamawa; and the south, to record traditional musicians who are getting very old and are the last repository of traditional music in Cameroon. In this episode of Afropop Worldwide, “Encounter With the Ancestors,” Georges Collinet takes us to Eric’s village in the deep forest of southern Cameroon to listen to his story. We also meet young musicians influenced by the art of their ancestors, including an opera singer!

videos.title: Georges Collinet Celebrates Half a Century of Radio Broadcasting
videos.description:
Born in Cameroon, Georges Collinet is one of the best-known and best-loved broadcasters on the African continent. Known to his fans as “Maxi Voom Voom,” Georges’ French and English language music programs on the Voice of America have attracted millions of listeners. Georges also hosts a television show connecting leading public policy and cultural figures around the continent.

Throughout his career, Georges has played a key role in connecting the U.S., Europe and Africa. Georges worked with African musicians in Paris during the ’70s and early 80s, supporting their efforts to retain African roots in their music and to develop a distinctive, professional sound. Since 1988, he has hosted Afropop and Afropop Worldwide, the award-winning series heard on public radio throughout the U.S., Europe and Africa.

videos.title: Tsapiky Homecoming
videos.description:
Tsapiky (tsa-PEEK) is an exhilarating, electric guitar driven dance music out of southwest Madagascar. A mix of South African pop and local Malagasy traditions, it is a modern sound, but one that has worked its way deeply into the region’s traditional culture. In recent decades tsapiky has largely replaced older folkloric styles as the music of choice at all-important ceremonies—typically funerals—at which extended families gather and party together for days on end.
 
In the spring of 2014, Afropop was lucky to be in Tulear when one of the greatest tsapiky guitarist/bandleaders, Damily, performed a free outdoor concert for the local, his first show there in 14 years. Tsapiky Homecoming, a video created by filmmaker Michal Shapiro and the Afropop team, tells the story of the music, the man (Damily), and this remarkable concert.  Enjoy!

videos.title: Seun Kuti Talks re: FELA! on Broadway With Afropop
videos.description:
In late December, 2009, Seun Kuti came to New York City to see the Broadway show FELA!, which presents the life of his late father, Fela Anikulapo Kuti.  Seun now leads his fathers band, Egypt 80, and along with his older brother Femi, carries Felas torch for a new generation of Nigerians.  Afropop was curious to know how Seun felt about seeing Felas life laid out on a New York stage.  Seun knows as well as anyone that Fela himself was extremely protective about his art and image.  In this exclusive interview, Afropops Banning Eyre, Sean Barlow, and Matt Payne spoke at length with Seun in his hotel room, and the conversation roamed well beyond the subject of FELA! on Broadway, to Seuns plans for a second CD, and even his opinions about films, Hollywood, Nollywood, and even Bollywood.

CAMERA: Chris Saddler   
EDITING: Julius Jusay

videos.title: Mandingo Ambassadors every Wednesday night at Barbes in Brooklyn
videos.description:
Afropop got to sit down with the Mandingo Ambassadors at Barbes where they play every Wedneday night at 10pm.

Here's what our senior editor Banning Eyre had to say about the Mandingo Ambassadors

"If you step into a New York club where the Mandingo Ambassadors (Ambassedeurs du Manding) are playing, and close your eyes, you go back in time, and across the Atlantic to Guinea, West Africa, in the 1960s. In the flush of Guineas independence from France, visionary African dictator Sekou Touré used music to forge a national identity. He funded bands from all over the country, selecting the most talented players through rigorous competitions, and nationalizing top bands in state-supported nightclubs in the capital, Conkakry. Although the Mandingo Ambassadors consist of four Guineans and four Americans (most of whom have studied music in Guinea), the sound is, as founder and lead guitarist Mamady Kouyaté proudly proclaims, 100-percent Manding with mellifluous, Latin-tinged rhythms and vocal melodies, and fleet, stinging electric guitar lines drawn from Guineas centuries-old traditions of Manding music." 
-Banning Eyre for Guitar Player Magazine

Our featured venue, Barbes, is a huge supporter of African music! It's a very homey, chill environment. Good drinks, great dancing! check out their current schedule for more shows at barbesbrooklyn.com

videos.title: Interview/New Music: Savannah V "talks about it" with Tejano Nation as her new single drops today
videos.description:
"Talk About It," a hip hop song in English that features heavy rapping and tough-talking lyrics, proves the impressive versatility of longtime Tejano artist Savannah V's voice as she tackles a style unlike any she's done before.

The story behind the song, which features rapper, Squishy, evolved from a surprising five little, but powerful, words that one female artist, diva, you could say, spoke against a fellow diva, whom she dismissed with: "I don't even know her."

Watch the interview here, or, for the complete package, visit TejanoNation.net to read the article and watch the masterfully done music video for "Talk About It," available today on all digital streaming platforms.

#talkaboutit #savannahv

videos.title: EXCLUSIVE INTERVIEW: Meet new artist Heather Jolene Alcantar
videos.description:
Meet San Angelo native Heather Jolene Alcantar, an aspiring Tejano artist whose first single release, "No Me Vayas a Dejar," flows fresh and flirty as a pop cumbia brimming with feel-good vibes and a reggae beat.

Alcantar chose to share her personal and powerful story with Tejano Nation first. 

And, while she did not choose the historic role she finds herself in as Tejano music's first transgender artist, this courageous and upbeat singer does not take the role, or the responsibility that comes with it, lightly.

videos.title: Michael Salgado Interview with Lilymarie
Interview: La Machy and Savannah V dare to swear w/premiere of collab, "CHATUM"
videos.description: This collaboration sparked interest from the start as both La Machy and Savannah V exude power, strength, and an edginess that makes people take notice. But, "CHATUM," the fourth single from La Machy, as a solo artist, featuring Savannah V, also an award-winning vocalist, will make many take notice. For many reasons. The language, yes, but more importantly, viewers will hear emotive voices and see passionate portrayals from two female artists you can't ignore. The two stars speak exclusively with Tejano Nation about the story behind "CHATUM," which stands for something you say when no other words will do. A few might say, "No, they didn't!" But most will sing along as they relate with the story behind the song.

videos.title: Interview: Stevie D gets real with Tejano Nation
videos.description: In an exclusive interview with Tejano Nation, Freddie Records artist and Tejano Music Award winner Stevie D shares the personal and devastating struggle that he battled for more than a year.  His perseverance and determination helped him persevere, and now, the popular and charismatic vocalist said he is both focused and ready to face the challenges that await him. And, he's highly motivated to please fans again with his distinctive voice and suave style.

videos.title: INTERVIEW: Stefani Montiel - Mis Favoritas, Vol. 2 (Ballads)
videos.description:
Popular, longtime Tejano artist Stefani Montiel talks to Tejano Nation about the six songs on her recently-released Vol. 2 of her EP series, "Mis Favoritas." Montiel, a versatile vocalist, re-creates the experiences of six classic and timeless Tejano ballads that evoke special memories in her life and career. Known for her energetic stage performances and danceable cumbias, Montiel celebrates an exciting career that spans three decades. 

The songs featured on "Mis Favoritas, Vol. 2 (EP)," include: "Si Quieres Verme Llorar," "Que Casualidad," "No Te Olvidare," "Entre Las Sombras," "Me Estoy Enamorando," and "Borracho de Besos."

videos.title: Interview: Nathan Acosta talks debut single, getting his break
videos.description: Talented, genuine, and gifted, accordionist/vocalist Nathan Acosta, 18, just released his debut single, "Solo," on the Freddie Records label with the worldwide release set for April 19, 2024. The mostly self-taught musician sits down with Tejano Nation to talk about how he got his start, what it's like to work and perform alongside two of Tejano music's most popular artists, Jesse Turner of Grupo Siggno, and Jennifer Pena, La Princesa de la Musica Tejana, and, recalls what happened exactly one year ago today that changed his life.

videos.title: Interview: Jaime DeAnda - Debut Solo Album, 'Volando Solo,' and new label NextGen Latinx Records
videos.description:
A trailblazer and trendsetter for the accordion sound and style, veteran Tejano/Conjunto artist Jaime DeAnda has captivated audiences for more than four decades with his master accordion skills, distinctive vocals, and high-energy dance moves. In 2018, after more than 30 years together, DeAnda and Los Chamacos, known as the premier conjunto showband, split in a move that shocked fans. 

However, DeAnda continued his journey as a solo artist, most recently, joining forces with a new label, NextGen Latinx Records, and releasing his first solo album, aptly titled, "Volando Solo". The much-awaited album will be available on all digital streaming platforms on April 5, 2024.  But fans can buy it now in either digital format so they get it immediately or order online at either nextgenlatinx.com or jaimedeanda.com and get it delivered.

DeAnda and NextGen Latinx Records CEO Mike Torres III talk with Tejano Nation about the new album, exciting future projects in the works for DeAnda's musical career, and even address his split from Los Chamacos, and his goal to always entertain his fans whether through his recordings or live performances.

videos.title: Teaser: Gary Hobbs Interview with Tejano Nation
videos.description:
See a few of the many highlights from our interesting and revealing talk as the longtime Tejano artist and fan favorite Gary Hobbs openly talks with Tejano Nation about everything from his latest single on Freddie Records, "Llegaste a Mi Corazon," written by Freddie Martinez, Sr., to his musical inspirations including Bruno Mars, yes, I said, Bruno Mars.

The smooth-voiced Hobbs,, of Eagle Pass,  boasts 40 years in the industry, and proved to be both an enjoyable and refreshingly candid  artist to interview. He is a unique mix of old-school Tejano  who promotes traditional values such as discipline yet he can easily talk about new Latin and pop artists like Karol G and Bruno Mars. And, he'll be on TikTok soon!

Don't miss the full interview and story, coming soon on  Tejano Nation

Hobbs is currently promoting his Latin Grammy nominated album, "Sin Fin."
Fans can catch Hobbs on social media, his podcast, and live at this year's Tejano Music Awards Fan Fair!!

videos.title: Pete Astudillo Interview - 022824
videos.description:
Tejano vocalist, award-winning songwriter, and energetic performer Pete Astudillo sits down with Tejano Nation to talk about his role in Tejano music history and his recent return to recording with a deeply personal song that will surely resonate within the Latino community. 

With humble and hard-working beginnings in the border town of Laredo, Texas, Astudillo recalls his struggles for recognition at the start of his music career, the once-in-a-lifetime opportunity  that let his talents shine as a singer, dancer, and composer with the iconic Selena y Los Dinos, and his own hit-producing solo career. Astudillo held a unique, front-row perspective as a member of Tejano music's most famous band led by the genre's brightest star.

videos.title: Kickoff Interview for the "Casate Conmigo 2024 Tour with Siggno, featuring Jennifer Pena"
videos.description: Hear straight from the stars of the "Casate Conmigo 2024 Tour with Siggno, featuring Jennifer Pena," as they share their excitement for the tour's kickoff this Friday, Feb. 9. with an additional show added, due to popular demand, for Saturday, Feb. 10, 2024, at San Antonio's Grand Event Center. Feel the love for their fans and the crazy chemistry as Grupo Siggno, led by Jesse Turner, welcomes the vivacious and talented Jennifer Pena into their circle. It is a concert experience you won't want to miss and is headed around the state, country, and even internationally, as these artists produce sounds that cross borders and get you moving. Another exclusive Tejano Nation interview just for you!

videos.description:
Latin music is ascending in the U.S., and, in some surprising ways, much of the story behind the trend begins in Texas. On Viva Tejano, host J.B. Sauceda talks with legendary tejano artists and well-known tejano music fans about how the music has shaped their lives. It’s a nostalgic journey and a close look at the influences behind many of today’s biggest acts in música Mexicana.

Audio subscribers to Texas Monthly can listen to episodes one week early, and get access to exclusive bonus material. Visit texasmonthly.com/audio (https://texasmonthly.com/audio)  to learn more.
